title: Migrate a legacy helper off dplyr's defunct underscore verbs (string-based column selection)
source_relation: adapted: dynamic grouped summaries and data-masking name clash families, expressed as a repair of a delivered legacy function
difficulty_hypothesis: group_by_()/arrange_()/filter_() with string arguments were removed (defunct) in dplyr; the replacement requires the .data pronoun or across(all_of()) with strings. Ties, missing group keys and a column literally named like an argument are secondary traps.

mcp_relevance.rationale: The migration path from removed standard-evaluation verbs to the .data pronoun is a version-specific fact; function documentation for the installed dplyr and its programming vignette state it. The defunct-function error message itself names the replacements, and base R is a complete fallback.
mcp_relevance.information_need: Which dplyr functions are defunct and how to select columns by string in the installed version.
mcp_relevance.obtainable_without_mcp: partly: the error message names select()/filter()/arrange() and points to vignette('programming')

calibration_risks.ceiling: high for strong baselines: base R fallback
calibration_risks.version_sensitivity: high but recoverable from the runtime error
blockers: ceiling effect likely when an agent runs the legacy code first

pinned_evidence.observed: group_by_(), arrange_(), filter_() each raise: was deprecated in dplyr 0.7.0 and is now defunct
pinned_evidence.oracle: base-R order() with original-row-order tie break and ave() truncation
